discovery: Experimental discovery of the Higgs boson through the conception and construction of the ATLAS and CMS detectors at the LHC
motivation: The 2013 prize honoured the prediction of the Higgs mechanism. The experimental discovery that confirmed it has not been recognised. Peter Jenni (ATLAS), and Michel Della Negra and Tejinder Virdee (CMS), conceived these general-purpose detectors in the late 1980s and led their design against extreme requirements. They made decisive choices in calorimetry, muon systems and trigger architecture, which is what made the 2012 observations of H to gamma-gamma and H to ZZ to four leptons possible. Two independent detectors established the result at five sigma each, and it has since been confirmed with precise coupling measurements. The discovery completed the Standard Model and changed what physics beyond it must look like: every current bound on supersymmetry, dark matter and extended Higgs sectors is built on this particle. It was a collective achievement, but these three people's early physical insight and leadership are clearly identifiable. Their work set the standard for modern collider experiments.
